subject: Tier naming + customer messaging for workload-aware batching defaults (final)
body:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 3, 2026 at 9:12 AM PST
Subject: Tier naming + customer messaging for workload-aware batching defaults (final)

Need to close the loop today on tier naming + the customer-facing wording that goes into:
- public docs (redwood-docs PR)
- Console copy (tier dropdown + “why this profile” panel)
- Hosted API docs / SDK param description

Current proposed names (from last week’s thread):
1) Fast
2) Standard
3) Cost-efficient

Open items:
- Any remaining objections to “Cost-efficient” vs “Economy”?
- We need one consistent 2–3 sentence definition per tier that does *not* over-promise hard latency for every workload.
- We should explicitly call out streaming behavior (first-token latency priority) vs non-streaming.

Draft customer-facing definitions (v6) below. Please reply inline w/ edits by EOD; if no objections I’ll lock the copy and tell docs/Console to implement.

---
Fast (lowest latency)
Best for user-facing, interactive experiences. Prioritizes low tail latency and faster time-to-first-token for streaming, with conservative batching and stricter queue admission under load.

Standard (balanced)
Default for most production workloads. Balances latency and cost via moderate batching and caching, targeting stable p95 performance across typical traffic mixes.

Cost-efficient (lowest cost)
Best for background or throughput-oriented jobs where cost per token matters more than tail latency. Uses more aggressive batching and may trade higher p95/p99 latency for improved throughput.

FAQ snippet candidate:
“Do these tiers change data handling or logging?”
No. Tiers only change runtime scheduling/batching behavior; they do not alter request/response logging, retention, or data access controls.

Console microcopy needs:
- Dropdown helper text (one line)
- “Why this profile?” reason code explanation (short)

Attachment stubs:
- tier-messaging-copy-v6.txt
- console-tier-tooltip-copy-v3.txt

Thanks,
Nikhil
—
Nikhil Sharma
Product Management, Hosted API
Redwood Inference



From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 3, 2026 at 10:04 AM PST
Subject: Re: Tier naming + customer messaging for workload-aware batching defaults (final)

Names look good. I’d keep “Cost-efficient” over “Economy” (economy reads like airline seat class and we’ll get questions).

Suggested tweaks to avoid implied guarantees:
- Add “generally” / “designed to” phrasing.
- For Standard, avoid “targeting stable p95” in customer copy; keep that in SLO doc / benchmarks page. We can say “designed for predictable latency” and link to the SLO tiers page for specifics.

Proposed edits (tightened):

Fast (lowest latency)
Designed for interactive, user-facing experiences. Prioritizes low tail latency and time-to-first-token for streaming, using conservative batching and stricter queue admission under load.

Standard (balanced)
Recommended default for most workloads. Balances latency and cost with moderate batching and caching to deliver predictable performance across common traffic patterns.

Cost-efficient (lowest cost)
Designed for throughput-oriented or background jobs. Uses more aggressive batching to reduce cost per token and may increase tail latency compared to Fast/Standard.

Console dropdown helper text (one line each):
- Fast: “Minimize tail latency (best for interactive + streaming).”
- Standard: “Balanced default for most workloads.”
- Cost-efficient: “Lower cost per token; higher tail latency possible.”

On “Why this profile?”: if we show reason codes, we should map them to plain English. E.g.,
- “Tier default” → “Using your selected tier’s recommended settings.”
- “Override” → “Using an explicit override configured for this route/tenant.”
- “Overload mode” → “Temporarily adjusted to protect system stability under high load.”

If you want, I can add the reason-code → copy mapping to the PRD appendix.

-Aditya



From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 3, 2026 at 1:26 PM PST
Subject: Re: Tier naming + customer messaging for workload-aware batching defaults (final)

+1 to the names.

Two Dedicated/enterprise concerns to incorporate into the customer-facing copy:
1) Avoid implying that selecting Fast automatically upgrades the customer’s contracted SLA. Some customers will treat “Fast” as “SLA tier.”
2) We should state that Dedicated tenants can set route/tenant overrides and that overrides take precedence over defaults (without going deep into precedence logic).

Minor copy tweaks I’d like:
- Replace “stricter queue admission under load” with something less scary. Maybe “stronger protections under load”?
- In Cost-efficient, explicitly call out that it’s best for non-interactive and that streaming endpoints generally shouldn’t use it.

Suggested phrasing:
Fast: “…with conservative batching and stronger protections under load.”
Cost-efficient: “Not recommended for latency-sensitive or streaming endpoints.”

Also: can we add a one-liner in the docs right below the tier table:
“Your contractual SLA is determined by your plan; batching tiers affect runtime behavior only.”

Lauren
—
Lauren Bishop
Product Management, Dedicated
Redwood Inference



From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 3, 2026 at 3:47 PM PST
Subject: Re: Tier naming + customer messaging for workload-aware batching defaults (final)

Locking this. Final decisions + final copy below. I’ll update the docs PR + ping Console to use the same strings.

Decision: tier names
- Fast / Standard / Cost-efficient (no “Realtime”, no “Economy”)

Customer-facing definitions (final)

Fast (lowest latency)
Designed for interactive, user-facing experiences. Prioritizes low tail latency and time-to-first-token for streaming, using conservative batching and stronger protections under load.

Standard (balanced)
Recommended default for most workloads. Balances latency and cost with moderate batching and caching to deliver predictable performance across common traffic patterns.

Cost-efficient (lowest cost)
Designed for throughput-oriented or background jobs. Uses more aggressive batching to reduce cost per token and may increase tail latency compared to Fast/Standard. Not recommended for latency-sensitive or streaming endpoints.

Docs footnotes (add directly under tier table)
- “Batching tiers affect runtime scheduling/batching behavior only; they do not change data handling, logging, or retention.”
- “Your contractual SLA is determined by your plan. Selecting a batching tier does not change your SLA.”
- “Dedicated tenants may configure route/tenant overrides; overrides take precedence over defaults.”

Console copy (dropdown helper text)
- Fast: “Minimize tail latency (best for interactive + streaming).”
- Standard: “Balanced default for most workloads.”
- Cost-efficient: “Lower cost per token; higher tail latency possible.”

Console copy (“Why this profile?” mapping)
- Tier default: “Using your selected tier’s recommended settings.”
- Override: “Using an explicit override configured for this route/tenant.”
- Model constraint: “Adjusted to match model/hardware constraints for this deployment.”
- Overload mode: “Temporarily adjusted to protect stability under high load.”

Next steps
- I’ll push the wording to https://github.com/redwood/redwood-docs/pull/1882 today and request review from both of you.
- Ava: FYI this is the customer-safe version (no hard numbers). The SLO doc will carry the p95/p99 targets and the benchmark methodology will link from docs.

Thanks,
Nikhil
